notes:
## Content and sheet

The underlined heading 16 names Sigma_J et Sigma_{J,L}. There is no separate authorial folio or date. The thin lower-left 84 is a later hand's foliation. The main labels are (70)–(74); H's editorial cross-page remarks are not source text.

For a bande J of I, (70) defines Sigma_J inside X_J star by deleting the indicated intersection with interiors of T_i. The adjacent notes define bar J as the ideal generated by J and give X_J as a union. Formula (71) lists empty, singleton, total and ideal cases. The author explicitly qualifies the proposed presentation (72) with On trouve, sauf erreur. Its diagram has source Sigma_ij and two arrows to Sigma_i and Sigma_j. Formula (73) is labeled équivalence d'homotopie. Formula (74) defines dotted Sigma_J through a boundary, an image-union expression and a final limit with au moins 2 termes.

The top diagonal note proposes the quoted éclatés orientés viewpoint. The left NB at (72) describes a stratification of type J.

## Mathematical prompts and ink decisions

- The two stacked expressions in (70) are joined by upright equality strokes. Below, the left upright pair and union are cancelled, while a second upright pair, NB and the right X_J bases remain live; only their old superscripts are locally cancelled.
- Limits were checked with their whole expressions: the top note has a plain lower rule, (72) first has one arrowhead and then a plain rule, and the last (74) limit has two distinct right-facing tips. The doubled tip records the ink without assigning it an extra mathematical meaning.
- Both empty-set signs in (71) have phi's loop and descending stem. The glyph is retained; no mathematical change of meaning is asserted.
- The left NB says type J but ends j,h in I. The barred capital I is kept despite the indexing question. All four disputed second letters have h's stem and shoulder, not H's k.
- The target in the image term of (74) is capital Sigma_J, distinguished from the source's small j. The union bounds and the neighbouring rows were reread together.
- Two opening parentheses but only one closing curve are visible in (72); no balancing parenthesis is supplied.
- In the X_J margin note, two independent horizontal bars support =; adjacent vertical overtracing is not a third bar. The top-note terminal dotted Sigma is separately visible.
- The title has et. Upright (70) and (72) belong to the main displays beneath the diagonal notes, not to marginal prose. Crossing writing is not automatically cancellation.

## Doubts and limits

Idem pour, l'on déduit and ayant|avec remain narrow. The cancelled Sigma-like group, both old stars, the b-like glyph and the final d'un before (73) also remain doubtful; Par suite and the cancelled union are readable. No letter is supplied merely because the mathematics would require it.

These are transcription rereadings, not proof verification; check_events is empty. All four notes, cancellations, numbers and the complete diagram are included in the inventory and blind boxes.
### Blind reading corrections

The opening diagonal note has a single dash in the long Sigma index and includes etc. after the limit expression. The introduction to (72) reads On trouve, sauf erreur; the earlier On a même was not sustained by the connected strokes. The first map index in (72) is the literal s_j, beside b_ij. The final X in the marginal X_J identity has an unbarred J, unlike the barred J in the preceding union; that literal asymmetry is retained. Its crowded relation is now uncertain, and no mathematical repair is made. The two small diagram shafts have terminal return curls. Formula (73) writes homo- at the end of its upper line and topie below. Formula (74) has a square-ended lower bracket and a horizontal minus in the union bound beneath it; its main T bound uses a slash. The two tips under its last limit remain distinct. Several small words and a quantifier-like marginal sign remain explicitly uncertain. These are observations of ink, not new proofs of the claimed identities.
